sampling_model.design: A fixed two-block panel with deterministic factors, an untreated pre block, a treated post block, and Gaussian sampling noise.
sampling_model.units: All \(N\) labeled units are observed in every one of the \(T_0+T_1\) periods; \(N,r,s\) are fixed and known.
sampling_model.treatment: The realized intervention switches on after the break, and \(\beta_i\) is the time-averaged attributable contrast for labeled unit \(i\).
sampling_model.overlap: No assignment-overlap condition is invoked because treatment timing is fixed; identification is governed by \(\kappa_s(L)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The loading projector is inferred from \(T_0^{-1}Y_0Y_0^{\top}\); all procedures may use the full panel, and no subspace rate is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: We propose consistent and asymptotically normal estimation and establish statistical inference for the direct and interference effects averaged over post-intervention periods.

body.tldr: Sparse direct and spillover effects are decoded from a post-period mean through a loading subspace learned from the untreated pre-panel. Conditional on a nonempty primitive class with ordered loading and noise bounds and \(K\ge\sqrt r\), the paper derives a finite-sample globally honest confidence set and its sharp margin-indexed expected-diameter frontier, proves equality of global and margin-oracle rates throughout the weak-margin region, and establishes a maximal-margin adaptation gain in the \(N=3,r=s=1\) experiment once an explicit four-line classifier has error at most \(\alpha/2\). The central open theorem is the same-sample oracle characterization over the remaining nonempty margin strata, including disconnected loading components and finite classification transitions, without beta-min, post-factor excitation, distinct loading strengths, or an assumed subspace rate.

project_justification.gap: HeLiShiMiao2026 turns panel interference into sparse robust regression but relies on a majority-valid-controls count, asymptotic selection, and coordinatewise inference. Sparse-confidence theory assumes an observed design, while projector-confidence theory does not propagate geometry into a causal sparse-vector diameter frontier. No opened paper characterizes global-versus-margin-oracle honest diameter when the loading operator is estimated from the same fixed-factor panel.
project_justification.niche: The exact Gaussian subclass makes the two information channels visible: post-period noise perturbs the sparse decomposition, and pre-period noise perturbs the loading geometry. Constant post factors force lower bounds to pay for geometry only through the original pre observations, while maximal-margin strata may split into finitely classifiable components.
project_justification.fill: The project combines an exact pre-panel second-moment region based only on the signal-versus-noise gap, finite support enumeration, every-sample diameter control, compensated-rotation lower bounds, and component-aware Gaussian decision inversion. On every nonempty primitive class it delivers the adaptive frontier, the weak-margin oracle equivalence, and a rank-one maximal-margin result from an explicit four-hypothesis experiment; the finite same-sample oracle profile on intermediate nonempty margins remains the open kernel.

body.related_work: HeLiShiMiao2026, Introduction, Assumptions 1--4, Theorem 1, its proof, and Discussion, moves from contaminated donors to a factor-adjusted sparse outlier vector and applied direct-and-spillover targets. The present core is narrower in errors but sharper in inferential quantifiers; its global-honesty and adaptive-frontier theorems provide finite-sample joint coverage and a margin-indexed diameter frontier on this Gaussian subclass, not a replacement for their full mixing model. Wei2026, Sections 3--4, Lemma 1, Theorem 1, Theorem 2, and Conclusion, gives donor-classification-free sharp scalar partial identification by full-simplex reduction and Farkas certificates in a different envelope model; it informs the finite inversion architecture but is not a comparator the present point-identified model claims to tighten. NicklVanDeGeer2013, Theorems 3--5 and their testing reduction, and CaiGuo2017 supply composite-mixture lower-bound logic for sparse confidence procedures with observed random designs. CaiLow2004 supplies the ordered-modulus view of subclass-versus-union expected length, while EvansHansenStark2005 supplies confidence-set decision duality; neither identifies the four nuisance-profiled Gaussian loading hypotheses nor the pathwise post-inversion diameter used at the maximal rank-one margin. NaumovSpokoinyUlyanov2017, Theorem 1 and its Gaussian comparison proof, supplies the projector-confidence exemplar, but its i.i.d. covariance experiment differs from the deterministic normalized factor panel; here the relevant eigengap is only the \(d_{\mathrm{lo}}^2\) separation between the signal subspace and noise, so repeated nonzero loading strengths are allowed. ChandrasekaranEtAl2011 and FickusMixon2013 own the generic sparse-subspace and erasure-robust geometry, so the uniqueness lemma is supporting rather than headline novelty. GoffMbakop2026 shows how estimated linear-system solvability can be tested uniformly, but its coefficient regularity does not characterize the disconnected same-sample oracle frontier. The centered, normalized, and bounded deterministic factor paths, the post-factor envelopes, the latent-mean bound, and the bounded effect envelope are transparent restrictions of the present Gaussian subclass rather than conditions attributed to HeLiShiMiao2026.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The general oracle step is not established by the available modulus sandwich: upper and lower bounds evaluate sparse-compatible subspace moduli at different resolution constants, and that mismatch is material when a new loading component becomes statistically reachable. The explicit four-line result settles only \(\gamma=1/\sqrt3\) when \(T_0\ge\overline T\); short-pre-panel classification and all intermediate high-margin profiles remain part of the open question. A bounded numerical probe for \(N=8,r=2,s=3\) reproduced \(\kappa_3=0.06586041095768687\) for the supplied polynomial frame and found larger random margins near \(0.0842\), but it did not certify the maximal-margin component geometry in that dimension.
body.honest_scope: The class is a homoskedastic Gaussian subclass of HeLiShiMiao2026 with fixed \(N,r,s\), unknown deterministic factors, \(T_0\ge r+1\), ordered primitive bounds \(d_{\mathrm{lo}}\le d_{\mathrm{hi}}\) and \(\sigma_{\mathrm{lo}}\le\sigma_{\mathrm{hi}}\), and \(K\ge\sqrt r\). The centered, normalized, and bounded deterministic pre-factor path, the post covariance and centered-norm bounds, the latent-mean bound, and the effect envelope are proposal-specific restrictions with the application rationales stated in their assumption nodes. Every global-honesty and minimax-risk claim is conditional on \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), and every margin-specific claim is additionally restricted to nonempty \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(\gamma)\). Repeated loading strengths are allowed because projector control uses only the \(d_{\mathrm{lo}}^2\) signal-versus-noise gap. There is no post-factor covariance lower bound, beta-min condition, correct-support event, or oracle subspace. The global adaptive frontier and weak-margin equivalence are theorem obligations; the all-margin oracle profile is the first-class open question. Sanity reductions are explicit: at \(\gamma=0\) diameter saturates at the bounded-signal scale, with known \(L\) the post component reduces to ordinary Gaussian sparse-mean inversion, and for \(N=3,r=s=1\) maximal margin reduces to four lines and removes the oracle pre-panel term only when the explicit classifier fits inside the reserved noncoverage budget.
